body:
## Bug: a heading containing a hard break is corrupted on save — break becomes a literal backslash and the rest of the heading splits into a new paragraph

Found in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` (the markdown ⇄ ProseMirror codec), verified this run on main `95bfedb4` with a standalone probe crate carrying a verbatim copy of `src/web/markdown.rs` (comrak 0.56; probe logs in the goal workspace `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-27-creator-a2/out3.log` cases `setext-hardbreak-backslash` / `setext-hardbreak-spaces`, PM-side case `heading-hardbreak` in `out2.log`).

### Reproduction (pure markdown in, no editor tricks needed)

A setext heading is a multi-line paragraph, so it can contain a hard break:

```markdown
Title\
more here
=====
```

(or the same with two trailing spaces after `Title` instead of the backslash.)

1. Parse direction: `markdown_to_prosemirror` produces one heading node whose inline content is `text "Title"`, `hard_break`, `text "more here"` — the parse-side `NodeValue::LineBreak` arm (`markdown.rs:295`) emits `hard_break` regardless of the containing block, and placement validation (`markdown.rs:979`: `"paragraph" | "heading" => child == Placement::Inline`) accepts it, since `hard_break` is inline.
2. Save direction: the `hard_break` arm (`markdown.rs:1385`) builds a comrak `NodeValue::LineBreak` inside the `Heading` node built at `markdown.rs:1141`, and `format_commonmark` renders it as a backslash + newline *inside* the ATX heading line:

   ```
   # Title\
   more here
   ```

3. Re-parsing that saved file yields a **different document**: a heading whose text is `Title\` (a literal backslash character has been added to the user's text) followed by a new plain paragraph `more here`. The heading the user had is split in two and gains a stray `\`.

The same PM doc built directly in the editor (e.g. convert a paragraph containing a hard break into a heading — `heading` in `richSchema` is `inline*` content, `pkgs/id/web/src/editor.ts:46`) corrupts identically.

### Why this is a codec bug, not just a renderer quirk

A direct comrak parse → `format_commonmark` control renders the same bytes (probe `out4.log`, DIRECT cases) — comrak's renderer cannot spell a line break inside an ATX heading either. But the codec's contract is ProseMirror fidelity (cf. #1031, #1370), and here the **PM document itself** changes across one open → save cycle. The codec already solves exactly this shape of problem for table cells: #1017's `append_table_cell_child` (`markdown.rs:~1560`) degrades a hard/soft break to a single space because "a table cell is single-line content in markdown". A heading is single-line content in markdown for the same reason, and gets no such degradation.

### Suggested fix direction (triage decides)

Degrade `LineBreak` children of a `Heading` to a space in the save direction (mirroring #1017's table-cell handling), or equivalently normalize them in the parse direction, so a heading with a hard break saves as `# Title more here` and re-opens as the same single heading. Rejecting with a `ConversionError` would be worse than the space degradation (it would make the whole document unsavable).

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Title\` + newline + `more here` + `=====` (and the two-trailing-spaces variant) round-trips to a single heading containing `Title more here` (or an equivalent single-line spelling) — no literal backslash added, no paragraph split.
- [ ] A hand-built PM heading containing a `hard_break` saves without corrupting on re-parse; output is a fixpoint.
- [ ] Hard breaks in paragraphs still save as hard breaks (existing behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Regression test in `web::markdown` tests next to the #1017 table-cell tests; existing codec tests still pass.
